extraction.name: Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating instruction-following ability of large language models using prompts with verifiable instructions.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors created a set of prompts with verifiable instructions through four steps: generating base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions, using few-shot prompting to identify and remove illogical prompts, using another few-shot prompting approach to rephrase prompts for diversity, and manually checking and editing the rephrased prompts one by one. They also report that they scraped model responses through API calls for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Experiments, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Around 541 prompts containing one or more verifiable instructions, plus model responses from GPT-4 and PaLM 2 Small collected through API calls.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: GPT-4 responses were scraped in November 2023 and PaLM 2 Small responses were scraped in August 2023.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Prompts were synthesized by concatenating base prompts with verifiable instructions, filtering illogical prompts with few-shot prompting, rephrasing prompts with few-shot prompting to increase diversity, and manually editing the prompts. Responses were also transformed with eight verification transformations for loose accuracy, including removing markdown font modifiers, removing the first line, removing the last line, and combinations of these transformations.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Illogical prompts were removed and rephrased prompts were manually checked and edited. For loose verification, responses were normalized using transformation functions that removed markdown modifiers and optionally removed the first or last line.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The paper describes manual curation of prompts and automatic verification of whether responses followed each verifiable instruction. No human labeling protocol for annotations is described beyond prompt editing and checking.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper defines strict and loose instruction-following accuracy. Loose accuracy is computed using multiple transformed versions of each response to reduce false negatives, but the authors note this may introduce false positives.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Few-shot prompting was used to identify illogical prompts and rephrase prompts. Automatic verification functions and transformation-based loose checking were used to evaluate responses.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors released their code and prompts on GitHub and state that the list of verifiable instructions can be expanded trivially. No formal versioning, maintenance schedule, or deprecation policy is described.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper discusses that reliable instruction-following evaluation is important for the precision, safety, and reliability of LLM implementations, especially in crucial scenarios such as healthcare or autonomous systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that human evaluation can be biased and inconsistent, and that model-based evaluation can be biased or limited by the evaluator model. It also notes that loose verification may introduce false positives.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically. The benchmark currently has limited diversity and quantity of verifiable instructions and does not yet cover multimodal use cases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation benchmark for training-related assessment, testing, and comparison of large language models on instruction following. The paper also suggests future use for expanding prompts and multimodal evaluation.
